outline: This course introduces the fundamental concepts, mathematical modeling, and dynamic behavior of electric power systems under small disturbances. Emphasis is placed on synchronous machine modeling, excitation systems, small-signal stability analysis, and multimachine system dynamics. Students will learn analytical techniques and simulation methods used in modern power system stability studies and understand the impact of control systems on system stability.
schedule:
Wk1: Course introduction and rules.
Wk2~Wk3: Introduction to stability and mathematical models.
Wk4~Wk5: Synchronous machine fundamentals and electromechanical dynamics.
Wk6: Park's transformation and dq-axis machine equations.
Wk7~Wk8: Network modeling, per-unit system, state-space representation.
"Wk9: Midterm closed-book exam."
Wk10~Wk12: Small disturbance analysis.
Wk13~Wk14: Simulation of synchronous machines.
Wk15: Multimachine systems.
"Wk16: Final closed-book exam"
